title: Internal Sales Coordinator
description:

Package Description: Receptionist and Administrator Be the person who helps make primary care work for your Brighton community. For many of our patients, you'll be one of the first people they speak to when they need our help. That makes this much more than answering phones and booking appointments. At Allied Medical Practice, we're looking for a Receptionist and Administrator to join our team across School House Surgery and Church Surgery in Brighton. You'll help patients navigate our services, make sure information gets to the right people and support our clinical teams with the administration that keeps a busy GP practice running. Some days will be busy. Priorities can change quickly. You'll speak to people who are worried, frustrated or simply unsure where to turn. That's why we're looking for someone who is organised, calm, approachable and genuinely wants to help people. What you'll focus on Helping patients access the right care You'll be one of the first points of contact for our patients, whether they're speaking to us face-to-face or over the phone. You'll help with appointments, respond to queries and make sure patients are directed to the right person or service. Sometimes that means dealing with straightforward requests. At other times, you'll need to listen carefully, follow our processes and recognise when something needs to be escalated. Keeping the practice running smoothly There's a lot that happens behind the scenes in General Practice. You'll support the day-to-day administration that helps our clinical teams deliver care, including managing emails, correspondence, patient records and other administrative tasks. You'll need to be comfortable juggling different priorities while maintaining accuracy and confidentiality. Managing appointments and patient requests You'll book, amend and cancel appointments, helping us make the best use of the clinical time available. You'll also deal appropriately with urgent appointment requests and home visit requests, following practice procedures to make sure information reaches the right clinical colleague. Supporting prescriptions and referrals You'll support the processing of repeat prescription requests in line with practice procedures and help ensure they're dealt with efficiently. You'll also help process referrals from our GPs, making sure information is complete and sent to the appropriate service. Managing patient information Accurate information is essential to safe patient care. You'll help manage correspondence and hospital letters, update patient records, support new patient registrations and make sure information is coded, filed or passed to the appropriate member of the clinical team. You'll work with our clinical system, SystmOne, and maintain patient confidentiality at all times. Being part of the practice team You'll work closely with GPs, nurses, healthcare assistants, administrators and practice colleagues. Good primary care depends on people working together, so you'll communicate regularly with colleagues both within the practice and across other NHS and healthcare services. You'll be someone your colleagues can rely on to follow things through and get the details right. The kind of person who'll enjoy working here Our Brighton practices are developing and changing, so we're looking for someone who is comfortable being part of a service that continues to evolve. For this role, that doesn't mean we expect you to come in and transform General Practice. It means being willing to learn, being flexible when things change and approaching problems with a positive, practical attitude. You'll probably enjoy this role if you: Like helping people and providing good service Can stay calm and professional when someone is upset or frustrated Enjoy being busy and having a variety of things to do Are organised and pay attention to detail Can prioritise when several things need your attention Are comfortable using IT systems and learning new ones Can follow processes while using common sense Know when to make a decision and when to ask for help Work well as part of a team but can also get on with things independently Are dependable, punctual and take responsibility for getting things done Can adapt when priorities or ways of working change You don't need to know everything about General Practice on day one. What matters is that you're willing to learn, care about doing a good job and understand that even the smallest interaction can make a difference to a patient's experience. What you'll bring You'll need: A good standard of education, including Maths and English GCSE at grades AC or equivalent Experience working in General Practice or the NHS Practical experience of working with others Experience of working under your own initiative Experience using IT systems in a working environment Experience using clinical systems such as SystmOne or EMIS Excellent verbal and written communication skills Confidence dealing with people face-to-face and over the phone The ability to resolve problems calmly, including when under pressure Good time management and the ability to work to deadlines Strong organisational skills and the ability to prioritise and multitask A good understanding of confidentiality and the importance of protecting patient information A flexible, reliable and professional approach to work It would be great if you also have experience in customer service, understand basic medical terminology or have experience coding or summarising medical records. The environment you'll work in Allied Medical Practice operates across School House Surgery and Church Surgery in Brighton. You'll be joining at an important time for our Brighton practices. We're continuing to develop the way our teams work together and strengthen links across our wider Sussex primary care services, helping colleagues share knowledge, experience and support. Our practices are busy and our patients have a wide variety of needs, so no two days will be exactly the same. You'll be part of a team that is focused on providing a good service to our patients while continuing to improve how we work. Who are we? We are Integrated Care 24 (IC24), the leading not-for-profit Social Enterprise providing innovative and patient-focused primary care services. IC24 is committed to improving access to health and social care for our patients and reducing demand on secondary care services. We provide services to over six million patients, including GP Out of Hours, NHS 111, Primary Care and Integrated Urgent Care services. Every day, our people help patients access the care they need, when they need it most. What's in it for you? Hourly pay rate of £12.71 6.6 weeks of annual leave per annum Access to the NHS Pension Scheme Learning and development opportunities to support your career journey Employee Assistance Programme including free 24/7 counselling support Access to health and wellbeing initiatives Blue Light Card discounts Colleague recognition and reward schemes The opportunity to make a real impact within a growing Social Enterprise Location: Allied Medical Practice School House Surgery & Church Surgery, Brighton Hours: 32 hours per week We celebrate brave ideas and brave people. Due to the nature of this position, employment is subject to proof of eligibility to work in the UK, a satisfactory standard DBS check and satisfactory references. We have a duty to safeguard, protect and promote the welfare of those who use our services and our employees. This means we take every step we can to protect people from harm, abuse and neglect. We are committed to providing equal opportunities for all and encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, including ethnic minority communities, disabled people, LGBTQ+ communities, neurodiverse individuals and other under-represented groups. We're committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone feels they belong. If you require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, please contact the recruitment team. title: Medical Secretary/Personal Assistant
description: An exciting opportunity has arisen to join our team at Seaside View Child Development Centre, based at Brighton General Hospital. We are looking for a motivated and organised individual to provide high-quality administrative support to our Community Paediatricians. This is a varied and rewarding role where you will work as part of a dynamic multidisciplinary team, gaining experience across a range of administrative functions within a supportive environment. This position is fixed term (18 month), and part time (25 hours per week). Please note: Due to recent changes in UK immigration and visa rules, this role may not be eligible for Skilled Worker visa sponsorship. Applicants who do not currently have the right to work in the UK may not be considered. Candidates requiring sponsorship should review the eligibility criteria on the gov.uk website before applying to assess their eligibility for a Certificate of Sponsorship for this role. Skilled Worker visa: going rates for eligible occupation codes - GOV.UK Health and Care Worker visa: If you'll need to meet different salary requirements - GOV.UK Provide comprehensive administrative support to Community Paediatricians, ensuring smooth day-to-day service delivery. Manage busy clinical inboxes, handle enquiries, and respond to requests in a timely and professional manner. Coordinate and schedule clinics, meetings, and appointments, ensuring accurate and efficient diary management. Prepare and process clinic documentation, letters, and reports, maintaining high standards of accuracy and confidentiality. Maintain and update patient records on relevant NHS systems, ensuring data is recorded accurately and in line with information governance requirements. Liaise effectively with internal teams, external agencies, and families to support seamless communication and service coordination. Assist in the monitoring of service performance indicators and contribute to the continuous improvement of administrative processes. Provide general reception or office support as needed, helping to ensure a welcoming and efficient environment. The post holder will provide a professional administrative support service to the Community Paediatricians. The post holder will be expected to work independently using their own initiative to ensure daily tasks and on-going responsibilities are prioritised and completed within agreed timeframes. The key requirements of this interesting and varied post are an attention to detail to maintain high standards of administrative support in a busy medical team whilst retaining a calm and flexible approach. Willingness to work as part of a team, provide cover for colleagues and share common tasks is essential. This role will act as a point of contact for any communication or correspondence relevant to the Medical Team and their direct reports. The main aspects of the role include sensitive communication with families and stakeholders, diary management, planning and organising of clinics, liaising with other agencies, accurate detailed documentation on to our patient database, managing waiting lists and caseloads to ensure an effective efficient service delivery. If all of this sounds exciting and, having read the job description and person specification, you think this is the right role for you then we look forward to seeing your application.

title: Membership & Events Coordinator - Immediate Start
description:
Membership & Events Coordinator - Immediate Start

Location: Hove, East Sussex
Salary: 15 - 17 p/h (DOE) PAYE
Job Type: Part-Time, 2 Days per Week
Working Pattern: Office-based

The Role

As a Membership & Events Coordinator, you will play a key role in the day-to-day management of the association, ensuring members receive excellent support while helping to increase engagement, membership growth, and industry participation.

This is a varied and rewarding position combining administration, relationship management, event coordination, communications, and business development. It would suit someone who enjoys building professional relationships, taking ownership of projects, and working as part of a collaborative team.

Key Responsibilities:

Membership Management
- Maintain accurate membership records and manage renewal processes.
- Act as the first point of contact for member enquiries.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with existing and prospective members.
- Support initiatives aimed at growing membership and increasing member engagement.

Events & Member Engagement
- Coordinate online events, webinars, and member engagement activities.
- Research and identify relevant speakers and industry topics.
- Manage event communications, registrations, and follow-up activities.
- Arrange committee meetings and prepare supporting documentation.
- Support regular member communications and updates.

Business Development & Partnerships
- Identify and engage with potential industry partners, suppliers, and sponsors.
- Build relationships with external stakeholders to support membership growth.
- Assist with initiatives designed to increase engagement and commercial opportunities.

Administration & Communications
- Update website content, news articles, and member information.
- Monitor industry developments and identify topics relevant to members.
- Support the delivery of member services and communications.
- Maintain accurate records and ensure the smooth administration of the association.

Skills and Experience

Essential
- Previous experience within membership services, events, legal, recruitment is ideal.
- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.
- Strong organisational skills with exceptional attention to detail.
- Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities.
- Confidence interacting with professionals and senior stakeholders.
- Strong IT skills, including Microsoft Office applications.

Person Specification

The successful candidate will be highly organised, proactive, and personable. You will enjoy building relationships, managing varied workloads, and working collaboratively to deliver an excellent experience for members and stakeholders. title: Reception Administrator
description: We are a large NHS Mental Health Trust in South East England. We're looking for people to help us provide high quality services for the patients, carers and local communities we serve. We want patients and staff to recommend our organisation as a place where they would be happy for their friends and family to be treated. You can help us do this by bringing your skills, experience and commitment to Sussex Partnership. We are looking for an enthusiastic, self-motivated and experienced part time receptionist. You will be based to work at Hove Polyclinic, First floor on the Millview Hospital site in Nevill Avenue, Hove. The post holder will look forward to a varied and rewarding work environment, in which finding a balance between team working and utilising initiative is important. You will need the ability to foster positive working relationships & in return be an essential part of the team. The post holder will be motivated and able to organise their workload, demonstrate a professional face to face and telephone manner, and be able to liaise effectively with other agencies and members of the public. The successful candidate will provide reception duties (checking in clients, taking in deliveries, liaising with team staff, booking rooms, taking calls etc) and general office tasks to support the admin team. An ability to deal sensitively with people who may be distressed at times is also essential. To deal with all incoming telephone calls and sign post as required To ensure post both internal and external is sent to the correct staff/team To be responsible for locking up at the end of the day To deal with all room booking requests via a generic inbox and booking resource scheduler system To support the wider team with duties such as Uploading Calling service users to advise prescriptions are ready for collection Photocopying see job description for further information
